message.content: {"caption":"Workflow diagram showing how matched skill/no-skill executions are diagnosed, checked against task constraints, and revised into an evolved skill.","description":"The diagram has three connected panels. In Setup, the input is T·W·S₀ (task, workspace, initial skill). A Task Interpreter reads explicit constraints from T. A Task-Compiled Verifier is compiled once from T and remains locked. Matched-run setup uses the same T and W and a frozen agent π, varying only whether S is loaded. Its connectors branch to paired executions: “with Skill S, τw” and “without Skill, τwo.” The robot icons represent the agent in those executions; document icons indicate task or execution artifacts. The paired executions feed Compare and diagnose. PACE compares them across Process Adherence, Artifact Evidence, Consistency, and Effectiveness Delta; a downward arrow leads to PACE output, which marks passages to edit or protect and locks the choice of Refine or Repair for the first pair. A marker icon denotes passage marking. The locked-verifier information also feeds a Verifier check that checks explicit task constraints; its lock icon denotes the fixed constraint check. PACE output and verifier-check connections lead into Edit and check. The verdict-to-action row maps “helped” to “edit,” “inert” to “defer,” and “hurt” to “reject.” Under Skill Iterator, Refine preserves the working workflow and deletes, clarifies, or corrects local defects; its funnel-like icon denotes refinement. Repair replaces conflicting procedures and adds missing execution information; its wrench icon denotes repair. The PACE and verifier results inform this edit/check stage. A bottom feedback connector routes candidate skill S′ back toward comparison/checking, while the revised output is shown as evolved skill S*.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
